Looks like it records on VHS. That means it's just writing a regular old TV signal to tape, NTSC or PAL depending on region. Which would make things super easy. Find the tape write head and trace back to find where in the support circuitry they come from, and see if you can cut and tap those signals and route it to a USB video capture device plugged into a computer-on-board device like the ODroid or Raspberry Pi, that can run Linux and capture software.

Don't forget to find the button signals and route them through GPIO to trigger start and stop capture, wake and sleep, things like that. Getting rid of the tape handling and hardware should leave lots of room, but expect to have to fabricate some mounting hardware to keep your bolt-ons in place. There's definitely going to be some extra signals you'll have to take care of to keep the video camera circuitry from detecting that it's hands have been chopped off and refusing to work, but sniffing signals while it's on should be pretty straightforward.
